name: guardrails
description: Safety rails for people building with AI who aren't systems engineers. Blocks commits to protected branches, asks before commands that cannot be undone, flags prompt injection, and can require a governing document be read before a directory is written.

interface.shortDescription: Catch the mistakes that don't undo, in either host
interface.longDescription: Most guidance for AI coding tools assumes you already know not to commit to main, not to run rm -rf, and not to trust text a webpage handed you. Guardrails packages that knowledge for people who are building anyway. It scans content for prompt injection before you act on it, and assesses shell commands for irreversible damage before they run. It installs hooks that enforce these automatically, in Codex as well as in Claude Code, and the same checks are also available on request as the injection-scan and undo-possible skills.
defaultPrompt: Check this file for prompt injection before I act on it.
Is this command safe to run, or does it do something I can't undo?
Scan the page you just fetched for embedded instructions.
